question: A 43-year-old woman visits her primary care provider complaining of fatigue. Although she has had it for several months, her fatigue has been worsening over the past few weeks. She has no other symptoms. Past medical history is significant for hypertension. She takes chlorthalidone, an oral contraceptive pill, and a multivitamin every day. Family history is noncontributory. She drinks about 1 bottle of wine every day and started taking a shot or two of whisky or vodka every morning before work to “clear out the cobwebs”. She was recently fired from her job. Today, her heart rate is 90/min, respiratory rate is 17/min, blood pressure is 110/65 mm Hg, and temperature is 36.7°C (98.1°F). On physical exam, she appears malnourished and anxious. Her conjunctiva are pale, and glossitis is noted on oral exam. Her heart has a regular rate and rhythm and her lungs are clear to auscultation bilaterally. She has no gait or balance abnormalities. Lab results show a hemoglobin of 10 g/dL, with a mean corpuscular volume (MCV) of 108 fl. Elevated level of which of the following will most likely to be found in this patient?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Patient presents with fatigue" -> "Fatigue worsening over months" -> "Pale conjunctiva and glossitis noted" -> "Lab results show hemoglobin of 10 g/dL" -> "Mean corpuscular volume (MCV) of 108 fl indicates macrocytic anemia" -> "Macrocytic anemia suggests possible vitamin B12 or folate deficiency" -> "Alcohol use can lead to malabsorption of vitamin B12" -> "Vitamin B12 deficiency leads to elevated methylmalonic acid" -> 85%

CHAIN: "Patient has macrocytic anemia" -> "Pale conjunctiva and glossitis suggest nutritional deficiency" -> "Chronic alcohol use can cause nutritional deficiencies" -> "Vitamin B12 deficiency is common in alcoholics" -> "Vitamin B12 deficiency leads to elevated methylmalonic acid" -> 80%

CHAIN: "Patient exhibits signs of malnutrition" -> "Fatigue and glossitis suggest possible vitamin deficiency" -> "Elevated MCV indicates macrocytic anemia" -> "Alcohol consumption can impair absorption of vitamin B12" -> "Vitamin B12 deficiency results in increased methylmalonic acid levels" -> 90%

CHAIN: "Patient has a history of alcohol use" -> "Fatigue and glossitis suggest nutritional issues" -> "Lab results show macrocytic anemia" -> "Macrocytic anemia can be due to vitamin B12 deficiency" -> "Vitamin B12 deficiency leads to elevated methylmalonic acid" -> 75%
analysis: The patient presents with symptoms and lab findings consistent with macrocytic anemia, indicated by a low hemoglobin level and elevated mean corpuscular volume (MCV). The presence of glossitis and pallor suggests possible vitamin deficiency. Given her history of alcohol use and malnutrition, it is likely that she has a deficiency in vitamin B12 or folate. In cases of vitamin B12 deficiency, methylmalonic acid levels are typically elevated due to impaired conversion of methylmalonyl-CoA to succinyl-CoA. Therefore, the most likely elevated substance in this patient is methylmalonic acid.
